chunks: What the Shaykh—may Allah, the Exalted, support him—informed me of, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from a number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿĀmir al-Qaṣabānī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bukayr, from his father, who said:

Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام said to me: “If you are certain that you have performed wudu (ablution), then beware of initiating a new wudu (ablution) ever, until you become certain that you have invalidated it.”

Then he said—may Allah, the Exalted, support him: Likewise, if one is certain of hadath and doubts taharah, then it is obligatory upon him to renew taharah so that certainty of it may be attained for him. No salat (prayer) suffices for him while he has doubt concerning the taharah required for it. So he should know this chapter so that action may be based upon it. We have explained that it is binding upon a person not to enter into salat (prayer) except while in a state of purity; therefore, when he is certain that he had invalidated his state, he should not turn away from this certainty except by the attainment of taharah for him.

key_terms.اسْتِئْنَافُ: renewing or recommencing an act from the beginning
key_terms.الْيَقِينِ: certainty, which serves as the operative legal basis here
key_terms.وُضُوءًا: wudu (ablution), the ritual washing before worship

ai.seo_question: If I doubt whether my wudu (ablution) is still valid, do I need to repeat it before salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes a legal principle regarding ritual purity: certainty is not overturned by doubt. Whoever is certain of having wudu (ablution) does not lose that ruling through mere doubt, while whoever is certain of hadath must restore taharah before performing salat (prayer).
